label: Women Vote Nationwide For President
detail: Women in every state may vote for president in 1880, and they turn out much as men of their own group and region do.
assumption: Adult women of every group and region are added to the electorate, borrowing the observed turnout and vote choice of men of the same group and region, discounted for a lower first-time turnout.
facts_text: Women in every state are lawfully entitled to vote for presidential electors in the election of 2 November 1880.
State laws and the courts have recognised the right of women to cast ballots for president on the same terms as men.
research_questions: How did women vote in Wyoming and Utah territories, where they could vote in the 1870s, compared with men there?
What share of eligible women turned out in municipal and school elections in states that allowed partial suffrage by 1880?
How did Black women in the South and immigrant women in northern cities vote relative to men of their own group?
Did the temperance and suffrage movements shift women's votes toward any party or third-party candidate?
source_text: Women can vote for president in every state in 1880.
